\section{Motion}
\begin{frame}{Position and velocity}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Position $x(t)$ is where the object is.
    \pause
    \item Velocity is $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$.
    \pause
    \item Acceleration is $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}
  \frametitle{Constant acceleration}
  \framesubtitle{The four equations}
  \begin{align*}
    v &= v_0 + a t \\
    x &= x_0 + v_0 t + \tfrac{1}{2} a t^2
  \end{align*}
  \only<2>{Only on slide two: $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2a\Delta x$}
  \uncover<3->{A closing remark.}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Blocks}
  \begin{block}{Definition}
    The average velocity is $\bar v = \Delta x / \Delta t$.
  \end{block}
  \begin{alertblock}{Careful}
    Direction matters.
  \end{alertblock}
